title: Ideal sheaf of a base-changed closed subscheme
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $i:Z\to S$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_S$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and let $g:Y\to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Then the projection $q:Z\times_SY\to Y$ from the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] is a closed immersion, and its ideal sheaf $\ker(\mathcal O_Y\to q_*\mathcal O_{Z\times_SY})$ is the image of the composite morphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules $$g^*\mathcal I\xrightarrow{g^*(\mathcal I\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_S)}g^*\mathcal O_S\xrightarrow{\epsilon_g}\mathcal O_Y,$$ where $g^*$ is the pullback of modules [def-pc-module-pullback] and $\epsilon_g$ is the morphism adjoint to $g^\sharp:\mathcal O_S\to g_*\mathcal O_Y$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01JU (lemma-fibre-product-immersion), part (1), second sentence: '$X\times_SY\to Y$ corresponds to the sheaf of ideals $\Im(g^*\mathcal{I}\to\mathcal{O}_Y)$'

proof.text: The projection pullback.snd i g is a closed immersion by the Mathlib base-change instance [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Pullback symmetry, invariance of the kernel ideal under an isomorphism on the source, and IdealSheafData.ker_fst_of_isClosedImmersion identify its kernel ideal with i.ker.comap g.

Let T be tensor pullback, adj the adjunction selected in the statement, and epsilon the adjoint structure-sheaf map. Comparing adj with the canonical tensor adjunction by leftAdjointUniq expresses epsilon as an isomorphism followed by tensorPullbackObjUnitToUnit. Thus epsilon is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf].

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-ideal-product-image] with J=i.ker and G=O_S, which is quasi-coherent. Multiplication J tensor O_S -> O_S is the ideal inclusion precomposed with the right unitor. Its image inclusion is the product inclusion. Tensor pullback is a left adjoint, hence preserves the epimorphism from the multiplication source to its image; precomposition with this epimorphism, or with a unitor isomorphism, leaves the image unchanged. Therefore image(T(j) followed by epsilon) equals image(T(J O_S inclusion) followed by epsilon). Transport the cited image equality along epsilon using Subobject.exists; image pushforward commutes with composition by the epi-image factorization.

For any monic ideal inclusion k:I -> O_Y and any isomorphism epsilon:M -> O_Y, naturality of the left unitor and whisker exchange express multiplication I tensor M -> M followed by epsilon as I tensor epsilon followed by multiplication I tensor O_Y -> O_Y. The latter is the right unitor followed by k. Both preceding maps are isomorphisms, so this composite has image Subobject.mk k. The image inclusion defining I M has the same image after epsilon, since the corestriction to an image is epi. Apply this elementary calculation with I=(i.ker.comap g).toModules and M=T(O_S), then substitute the kernel-ideal equality from step 1. This is exactly the stated image equality.
